# Results — Study 634 (US-Leads-the-World, "America sneezes")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **today's
US close predicts tomorrow's Tokyo, Frankfurt, London and Sydney sessions** (the time-zone
spillover: by the time the Nikkei rings its opening bell, the full US day is public
information) — tested as a predictive regression of each overseas market's **next session**
on the SPY day-t close-to-close return, 1997 → 2026. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial July 2026 is dropped). Fingerprint `c6ad53f6345c`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **Open + Close** bars — **SPY** (total-return adjusted) + **^N225 / ^GDAXI / ^FTSE / ^AXJO** (cash indices, **price-only** levels) |
| Window | 1997-01-02 → 2026-06-30 (**29.5 years**; 7,673 dates × 5 tickers; 7,415–7,417 aligned US-day → next-foreign-session pairs per market) |
| Alignment | each US day *t* is paired with the **first foreign session strictly after** date *t* (Tokyo/Sydney open 2–3 h after the NYSE close; Frankfurt/London the next morning) — the predictor is fully public **before** the target session begins, exactly **one** execution lag by construction |
| Open quality | Yahoo index **opens are stale** (open = previous close) in stretches: ^FTSE **88%** stale, ^AXJO **41%** stale, ^N225/^GDAXI ~0%. Every open-based leg (gap/intraday split, the feasible trade) is measured on **live-open days only** and the share is quoted next to the number |
| Execution / costs | the only feasible trade enters at the **next foreign open** (the overnight gap is forfeit — it prints before any order can fill); one round trip per day at **5 / 10 bps one-way** |

> **Survivorship:** none of consequence on the Signal axis — the panel is four headline
> national indices (not a picked basket), all continuously computed through the window.
> The indices are **price-only** (no dividend adjustment on Yahoo); on daily
> return-on-return slopes the dividend drift is negligible, but it is labeled everywhere.

## The signal — tomorrow's session on today's US close (OLS slope, Newey-West HAC *t*)

| market | slope | HAC *t* | R² | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ^N225 — Nikkei 225 (Tokyo) | **+0.561** | **+19.59** | 20.0% | 7,415 |
| ^GDAXI — DAX (Frankfurt) | +0.222 | +9.21 | 3.5% | 7,417 |
| ^FTSE — FTSE 100 (London) | +0.230 | +10.50 | 6.2% | 7,417 |
| ^AXJO — ASX 200 (Sydney) | +0.387 | +11.18 | 23.2% | 7,417 |
| **GLOBAL-4 equal-weight basket** | **+0.350** | **+14.85** | **19.5%** | 7,417 |

A 1% US day moves the next Tokyo session **+0.56%** on average and the four-market basket
**+0.35%** — with HAC *t*'s of **9 to 20**, this is one of the strongest signals the desk has
ever measured. The 50-seed **shuffle placebo** (US predictor randomly permuted; a random
baseline averaged over ≥ 20 seeds per house rules) collapses to mean |slope| = **0.0070**,
mean |*t*| = **0.75** — the time link, not the marginals, carries the whole effect.

## Mechanism — the spillover lands in the overnight gap, before you can trade

Next-session return = **overnight gap** (previous foreign close → open, prints before the
first tradable tick) + **open→close** (the only leg an open-entry trader can own). Live-open
days only:

| market | gap slope (t) | gap R² | open→close slope (t) | oc R² | gap share of slope | live opens |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ^N225 | +0.368 (+21.15) | **38.2%** | +0.193 (+6.66) | 4.1% | **66%** | 100% |
| ^GDAXI | +0.158 (+6.94) | 8.6% | +0.066 (+4.11) | 0.4% | **71%** | 100% |
| ^FTSE | +0.139 (+7.56) | 23.2% | +0.147 (+5.05) | 2.9% | 60% | **12%** |
| ^AXJO | +0.194 (+14.67) | 27.0% | +0.251 (+16.53) | 16.5% | 50% | **59%** |

Two-thirds of Tokyo's spillover is delivered **at the opening print**: the gap regression's
R² is **38%** — the Nikkei open is close to a deterministic function of the US day. What
leaks into the open→close leg is small where opens are honestly recorded (DAX oc R² =
0.4%) and **inflated where they are not**: the ASX index "open" is built from a staggered
10-minute opening auction (stocks not yet open carry the previous close), so part of the
measured "intraday" drift is repricing that happened **before any order could fill**. The
^FTSE decomposition rests on the 12% of days with live opens (mostly 1997–99 and 2025–26)
and is quoted for completeness only.

## Decay by era — GLOBAL-4 basket

| era | slope | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1997–2003 | +0.336 | +17.56 | 1,760 |
| 2004–2010 | +0.410 | +15.88 | 1,763 |
| 2011–2017 | +0.429 | +10.99 | 1,761 |
| 2018–2026 | **+0.266** | **+4.49** | 2,133 |

The spillover has **not** died — three decades after Hamao-Masulis-Ng documented it, the
latest era still clears *t* = 4. It softened after 2018 but remains decisively positive.

## Conditional on the size of the US move — |SPY| quintiles, GLOBAL-4

| quintile (mean \|US\|) | slope | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 (0.09%) | +0.322 | +1.83 | 1,484 |
| Q2 (0.29%) | +0.259 | +4.37 | 1,483 |
| Q3 (0.57%) | +0.407 | +10.46 | 1,483 |
| Q4 (0.97%) | +0.380 | +15.57 | 1,483 |
| Q5 (2.18%) | +0.343 | +12.51 | 1,484 |

The slope is **flat across move sizes** (~0.26–0.41): the world does not need a big sneeze —
it reprices proportionally to whatever the US did. (Only Q1's *t* dips below 2: on ±0.1%
US days there is almost no signal to transmit.)

## Third axis — does the spillover survive the post-2010 algo era?

Pre/post-2010 slopes, with a *t* on the **difference** (HAC SEs combined in quadrature):

| market | pre-2010 slope (t) | post-2010 slope (t) | decay t_diff |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| ^N225 | +0.544 (+16.2) | **+0.584 (+11.5)** | −0.66 |
| ^GDAXI | +0.247 (+9.0) | +0.190 (+4.7) | +1.16 |
| ^FTSE | +0.289 (+13.5) | +0.154 (+4.7) | **+3.42** |
| ^AXJO | +0.411 (+21.3) | +0.356 (+5.0) | +0.74 |
| **GLOBAL-4** | +0.373 (+21.4) | **+0.321 (+7.1)** | +1.06 |

**Confirmed — the algo era did not kill it.** The basket slope post-2010 is +0.321 at
*t* = +7.1 and the pre/post difference is insignificant (t_diff = +1.06); Tokyo's slope
actually *rose*. The one genuine decayer is **London** (halved, t_diff = +3.42 — the market
whose session most overlaps New York's and where cross-listed/futures arbitrage is
densest). The spillover persists because it is **information flow, not an inefficiency**:
the repricing happens at prints you cannot trade, so there is no P&L for algos to compete
away on the close-to-close definition.

## Tradability — the honest catch, in three layers

**Layer 1 — the phantom backtest.** Hold each foreign market close-to-close on the US
sign: ^N225 **+48.2 bps/day** (HAC *t* = +27.59), ^AXJO +35.3, ^GDAXI +20.9, ^FTSE +18.7.
**Infeasible** — the foreign close of day *t* prints *before* the US day-*t* close exists
(Tokyo closes ~01:00 ET, Europe ~11:30 ET). This is the time machine every naive spillover
backtest runs, quoted only to size the illusion.

**Layer 2 — the only executable trade.** Follow the US sign at the **next foreign open**
(you know SPY's close hours before Tokyo opens), hold open→close, one round trip per day,
live-open days only:

| market | gross bps/day (HAC t) | net @5 bps one-way | net @10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| ^N225 | +9.5 (+7.22, n=7,386) | **−0.5** | −10.5 |
| ^GDAXI | +5.0 (+3.58, n=7,381) | −5.0 | −15.0 |
| ^AXJO | +22.8 (+16.40, n=4,392) | +12.8 | +2.8 |

Tokyo and Frankfurt — the two markets with honestly recorded opens — **die at 5 bps
one-way**. The ^AXJO line *looks* alive, but its measured open is precisely the one that
is **not a tradable price** (staggered opening auction; the "open" embeds pre-open stale
constituents, crediting the trade with repricing no order can capture; its live-open
subsample is also era-skewed). Gross, daily-turnover, index-level: this is a Mirage line,
not a strategy.

**Layer 3 — the wrapper trap.** The US-listed wrappers (EWJ, EWG, EWA, EWU) trade **during
US hours** — their price at the US close already embeds the US day contemporaneously (they
are priced off futures/fair value). "Buy EWJ at the next US open after a US up-day" buys
the spillover **after** Tokyo has already opened, gapped and closed. The time zone that
creates the predictability is exactly what the accessible vehicle takes away.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic world with a **planted** overnight-spillover beta (US day-*t* → next-day
foreign gap); same pipeline end to end:

| planted beta | cc slope (HAC t) | gap slope (t) | oc slope (t) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (null), SYN_A | +0.003 (+0.25) | −0.003 (−0.60) | +0.006 (+0.49) |
| **0.00** (null), SYN_B | +0.007 (+0.51) | +0.002 (+0.48) | +0.005 (+0.37) |
| **0.35**, SYN_A | **+0.354 (+25.82)** | +0.347 (+72.86) | +0.006 (+0.49) |
| **0.35**, SYN_B | **+0.357 (+27.05)** | +0.352 (+78.00) | +0.005 (+0.37) |

With beta = 0 the detector finds nothing (|t| ≤ 0.51); with beta = 0.35 it recovers
**0.354–0.357** — the planted value — and correctly locates it **entirely in the gap**.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Today's US close predicts tomorrow's overseas sessions with slopes of
  **+0.22 to +0.56** and HAC *t*'s of **+9.2 to +19.6** per market (**+14.85** on the
  GLOBAL-4 basket, R² = 19.5%), a 50-seed shuffle placebo at |t| ≈ 0.75, stable across
  |US-move| quintiles and every era (2018–2026 still *t* = +4.49). One of the cleanest
  *t*'s on the desk's whole bench.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** 50–71% of the slope is delivered in the **overnight gap**, a
  print that exists before any order can fill; the only executable version (enter at the
  next foreign open) nets **−0.5 bps/day** (Tokyo) and **−5.0 bps/day** (Frankfurt) at just
  5 bps one-way; the one "surviving" line (^AXJO +12.8 net) rests on an index open that is
  not a tradable price (staggered auction, stale constituents); and the accessible US
  wrappers (EWJ/EWG) trade during US hours, where the spillover is contemporaneous, not
  predictive. Predictability without a vehicle.
- **"Survives the post-2010 algo era?" — CONFIRMED.** GLOBAL-4 post-2010 slope **+0.321**
  at HAC *t* = **+7.1**, pre/post difference insignificant (t_diff = +1.06); Tokyo's slope
  *rose*. Only London genuinely decayed (halved, t_diff = +3.42). The spillover persists
  because it is information flow priced at untradable prints — there is nothing for the
  algos to eat.
